output.brief: The Android drop is almost certainly caused by a new Corvane edge rule, not by release 6.14. A rule pack the vendor auto-applied on 3 March (10:38 UTC) added a rule, AUTO-LIB-17. It blocks password-login requests that come from the networking library the Android app uses. The first blocks were logged at 10:41, and the telemetry shows the first failures at the same minute. Those failures hit every Android version equally, 6.11 through 6.14, and every OS version, whether or not the March security patch was installed. Quick-unlock is unaffected, and so are iOS and web. Password success fell from 96% to 8%. The blocked requests come from about 41,300 installs, and 92% of those had logged in successfully before, so they look like real customers, not bots. A rollback of 6.14 would not fix this, and 6.14 is only 5–10% of traffic. Raising bot sensitivity or excluding blocked attempts from the KPI would make things worse or hide the problem. Next step: ask Corvane to switch the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path. Keep every other control on. Then confirm in telemetry that password success recovers. Tell the executive committee the cause is the vendor rule. The contact-centre rise is only loosely tied to the drop, because the fee notices also drove calls that week. Confidence is high.
